title: October home sales edge up amid overall flat housing market, according to CREA | CBC News
html:
Business·New

Canadian home sales edged up in October amid overall flat housing market: CREA

Numbers better than expected, but recent rate hike and overall economy keeping market slow

Home sales across Canada edged up slightly in October but remained below October 2025 levels, according to the Canadian Real Estate Association (CREA).

National sales in October were up 0.3 per cent month over month, but still down 10.6 per cent compared to October 2025.

"Not much activity between September and October," said CREA senior economist Shaun Cathcart. "But the remarkable part about that is that it ran counter to … a lot of analysts' — including ours — expectations."

Cathcart expected already slow housing sales to slump into the end of the year after the Bank of Canada raised its benchmark interest rate a quarter-point to 2.5 per cent last month, the first rate change in a year and the first rate hike since 2023.

Real estate experts have predicted the hike will keep cost-conscious potential buyers worried about the potential of rising mortgage payments on the sidelines.

Cathcart says he still expects sales will remain relatively flat nationally in the coming months while potential buyers perhaps wait to make a purchase until they get a better sense of where rates are going.

"It could be that we only get another maybe one or two hikes, and that once things sort of settle and we get a little bit more certainty next year, you can see the market come back stronger."

The average price of a home in Canada in October was $656,200, down 3.1 per cent from 12 months ago. The markets in Ontario and British Columbia continue to be slow, while the prairies and East Coast have been "hotter" than many people might be aware, Cathcart said.

But with one rate hike already and potentially more to come, he said, "I think you're going to see everyone sort of cooling off a little bit more."

There were 197,000 homes listed through MLS platforms country-wide at the end of October —slightly above the long term average, according to CREA.

With files from the CBC's Abby Hughes
summary: Home sales across Canada edged up slightly in October — defying the expectations of some analysts — but remained below levels from October 2025, according to the Canadian Real Estate Association (CREA).
